proposal.name: Gate sampled Python application checks and report actual evidence

issue_plan.name: Gate sampled Python application checks and report actual evidence
issue_plan.summary: Complete #327 in four ordered changes: prepare application sessions, check bound observations with TLC, report actual evidence, then connect the public gate and CLI with real integration tests and a manual example. Keep public execution guarded until the final change. Each issue maintains SPEC.md and README; the merger records new policy and completes unavailable Docker/network checks before moving on. Support explicit and omitted components, granting sampled testing evidence without proof or exhaustive coverage.

issues.title: Prepare validated Python application sessions with and without components
issues.body:
Issue #327 connects the Python application adapter from #315/#318 to the normal sampled verification gate. Establish shared capability validation and session preparation for explicit and omitted components. Keep verify.Check, verify.Run and Python.Check guarded for existing Python until the final issue.

Build on project.ResolvePythonApplication, project.ResolveComponents, verify.StagePythonApplication and PreparePythonApplicationSession in internal/project and internal/verify. Share capability validation between sessions and later public entry points. Validate the complete configuration before verification tools, image acquisition or dependency installation. Syntax discovery may use the existing isolated parser. Admit only Python existing applications and the supported sampled observation contract. Reject unsupported component languages/modes, proof selections even without proof invocations, unsupported invocation/evidence modes, incompatible or missing selections, mismatched manifest/selected drivers, targets inconsistent with existing selections and required configured tests or conformance checks without executable supported invocations. Invalid explicit configuration or no usable conformance must never fall back to legacy execution or pass vacuously. Inventory neighbors without selected checks remain legitimate unchecked components. Explicitly reject existing-Python exhaustive and attempted-step requests, never downgrade them to sampled success.

Retain the existing explicit invocation grammar: literal python, -m unittest followed by explicit dotted selections without discovery/options/implicit suites; conformance invokes the manifest's contained script from the declared working directory with literal ordered arguments and must execute the configured lexical driver. Retain reserved-environment validation and declared versus effective sampling, including existing defaults and maxima. Preserve the adapter's supported ordinary synchronous function/instance read-back contract and its rejection of unsupported observation bindings. A Nagini marker does not select proof in this application mode; no annotation or marker is required.

Support omitted components without inventing scope, component checks or an explicit inventory: ResolveComponents must still return legacy mode, and eventual reports must not acquire Components. Run the manifest conformance driver using the same trusted collector and establish actual execution provenance against selected existing sources, declarations and surrounding application entries. Resolve only the execution bindings needed for this contract, not an inferred production inventory. Every existing source selection must be accounted for by genuine bound execution; importing, touching, or calling selected code independently of a substitute reported lifecycle is insufficient. Preserve ordinary Python unittest discovery behavior for this no-components mode while recording actual executed tests and failures; this does not broaden the explicit-component invocation grammar. Legacy driver sampling uses the existing defaults. Preserve selected files/directories, full application resources and original source bytes.

Prepare a coherent session before any execution: stage and resolve application, tests, driver, manifest, lock, model and local include inputs first; expose the staged project/model context needed by later TLC and attribution so no consumer rereads originals. Validate reloaded staged configuration, freshness and path containment as well as caller configuration. Select the staged application's admitted dependency image exactly once, retain its immutable execution identity plus original/canonical requirements and wheel-resolution evidence, and use it for every command. Verification-local requirements cannot replace application-root requirements. Retain full-tree file hashes, detached views, offline linux/amd64 execution, startup/import precedence, effective hash seed 0, read-only inputs, no image fallback, resource limits and cancellation/Close cleanup. All failure paths clean private resources and leave original bytes unchanged.

Tests must cover supported explicit and omitted-component preparation, execution binding without invented inventory, no-tools preflight for unsupported configurations, selected checks without invocations, malformed explicit configuration without fallback, source/driver consistency, snapshot freshness and changes to originals after staging, one image selection across runs, and no proof preparation even for marked application files. Add meaningful actual-Python tests for the omitted-component path and its unused/import-only/substitute-lifecycle failures using the existing runner contract; orchestration doubles only supplement execution tests. Preserve existing explicit-session, discovery, dependency and collector security regressions.

Update SPEC.md and README in the same PR to describe the new session and validation capabilities and retain the public-gate limitation at this intermediate step. Do not edit decisions/, existing pinned statements or ratified locks. Foundations: D-0105, D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0047, D-0054, D-0158, D-0168, D-0177, D-0178, D-0180 and D-0181, with current documentation required by D-0122. Changed SPEC bullets cite their recorded foundations. The ratified #327 plan supplies the new policy pending merger decision recording. Decision recording and unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work, alone requiring no repair. Document real-test commands and require passing final-head output before proceeding.

issues.title: Check bound Python application observations against the sampled model
issues.body:
After the first #327 issue merges, build on its explicit and legacy application sessions. Add a directly callable sampled checking path over those prepared sessions, using actual Python execution and existing internal/conformance TLC trace checking. Public verify.Check, verify.Run and Python.Check remain guarded until reporting and final gate integration are complete. Return independent check results, not a full gate verdict.

Run required admitted test and conformance invocations from one prepared session. Use only its staged project, source, driver, model, local includes and lock snapshots and its single admitted dependency image. Translate authenticated, complete, implementation-bound initial and transition observations to the existing conformance trace representation without losing run boundaries, order, state values or target/check/invocation identities. Check actual initial states against Init and actual state-changing transitions against Next at the ratified bounds, preserving existing stuttering/refusal semantics, deterministic encoding and batched checking. Do not accept a plausible driver-written trace in place of the collector's execution/read-back evidence. Preserve exact numeric and scalar values through Python JSON and TLC encoding, and diagnose incompatible model variables or unsupported encodings rather than silently coercing them.

Return actual evidence for gate aggregation and receipts: the execution result and its provenance, declared and actual invocation/settings, per-test exercise/outcomes, raw bound observations, model/include and bounds identities, effective sampling, actual TLC pins and checks, actual counts, outcomes and diagnostics per exact target/check/invocation. Never create passing rows from planned invocations, successful process exits, or another check's execution. Required tests must have actually run and passed; failed, skipped, expected-failure, unexpected-success, fixture/import/runtime errors and unexecuted selected tests cannot qualify. Missing/malformed/incomplete evidence, unused/import-only targets, substituted targets or reported lifecycles, invalid starts/transitions and TLC failure cannot qualify. Diagnostics identify the check and missing evidence or failed condition.

Keep successful independent test or conformance observations when another required invocation fails, while the aggregate sampled-check result fails. Preserve valid partial runtime outcomes under the existing API contract; do not accept unauthenticated or invalid conformance streams as partial successes. Continue independent invocations where safe and return their results with failures rather than discarding all evidence at the first error. Cancellation and operational errors remain distinguishable from model violations and missing evidence. No assertions, target runtime coverage or proof are inferred. Only successfully checked sampled observations establish tested-against-the-model evidence; exhaustive-state and every-step qualifiers remain false and no larger-bound or every-size claim is made. Reject exhaustive/attempted-step requests at preflight and reject non-sampled evidence emitted at runtime.

Add acceptance and regression tests around the direct checking API with a real unchanged task-lifecycle application, sibling entry code and resource access. Real Python and TLC must demonstrate a valid lifecycle and a forbidden real transition, plus an invalid initial state. Cover unused/import-only targets, a driver that calls selected code but reports a substitute lifecycle, runtime/import errors, failing selected tests beside passing tests, skipped/unexecuted selected tests and malformed/missing output. Exercise explicit and omitted-component sessions. Add a case large enough to exercise batched trace checking and preserve deterministic results. Use orchestration doubles for call sequencing, no-tools rejection and forced transport failures only as supplements. Record source immutability and one retained dependency-image selection. Document the real Docker command; fail on missing prerequisites when requested. Passing final-head Python/TLC output is Merger work if unavailable in the factory.

Keep the existing conformance checker and legacy Python, marked-file Python, TypeScript and Go behavior intact. Do not invoke Nagini or any proof adapter, and do not connect factory drafting/synthesis. Update SPEC.md and README in this PR to describe directly callable sampled TLC checking, evidence limits and the still-guarded public gate. Cite D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0047, D-0054, D-0158, D-0168, D-0170, D-0171, D-0177, D-0178, D-0180 and D-0181 as appropriate on changed SPEC bullets (D-0122). The merger records this ratified plan's new policy and dependencies. Do not write decisions/ or change existing pins/locks. Recording and unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work, alone requiring no repair.

issues.title: Render actual Python application checks as independent receipt evidence
issues.body:
After the first two #327 issues merge, use their prepared sessions and sampled Python/TLC results. Connect those actual check results to verify.Report, the existing component attribution APIs and internal/receipt JSON/Markdown views, with portable complete fingerprints. Provide tested report assembly for direct checking; keep public existing-Python gate entry points guarded until the final issue.

For explicit inventories, populate components through AttributeComponentConformance and AttributeComponentRuntime using exact selected target/check/invocation IDs and actual execution/TLC results. Retain the whole explicit inventory including unchecked neighbors and files with no functions. Each component without its own qualifying conformance remains unchecked for conformance; every component without proof remains unchecked for proof. Keep configured assumptions visible as assumed/unverified. Runtime tests and any assertions qualify independently from actual exercise, outcomes and matching provenance, grant no target coverage and cannot be inferred from a process exit, invocation declaration, passing conformance or another selected test. The adapter currently provides no assertion evidence; do not invent it. Missing checks remain missing or explicitly diagnosed, never successful result rows. Preserve valid independent results when another check fails.

Record both declared invocation metadata and the actual interpreter/launcher, ordered argv, working directory, environment, effective sampling and pins. Preserve existing transactional attribution validation: incoming and retained evidence are revalidated, invalid/stale replacement is atomic, replacing or clearing one evidence kind preserves other kinds, and supplied rows alone never change Report.Passed. In particular, do not weaken invocation matching merely because actual launcher argv differs from the declared command; retain both in appropriately validated provenance. Add an explicit distinction between gate-produced execution evidence and externally supplied records in JSON and Markdown, including mixed/replaced evidence. External attribution must not accidentally inherit an executed-by-the-gate designation, and origin labels cannot replace provenance validation or become a gate verdict.

For omitted components, retain legacy inventory mode and omit component inventory/evidence. Add application execution provenance and actual test/conformance evidence without inventing production scope. Preserve receipts and fingerprints for preexisting legacy projects that have no new application execution data. New sampled application receipts grant tested-against-the-model evidence only for successful bound observations checked by TLC, never proof, exhaustive code-state coverage, every-step or project-wide every-size claims. Distinguish exhaustive design checking within bounds from sampled implementation checking.

JSON, Markdown and fingerprints must describe what ran and what TLC checked, not just intended commands and counts. Cover selected and unselected application files, resources, tests, driver, runner and observer bytes; dependency input/canonical/resolution and artifact evidence; model and includes; ratified bounds; declared and effective sampling; observations, counts, outcomes and diagnostics. Retain the immutable execution image identity where needed to audit the session while using portable content/resolution identity for deterministic hashing, excluding local image IDs/tags, timestamps, host paths and ephemeral execution/container/authentication IDs. Changing an observation or any relevant input must change the fingerprint even if all counts and pass/fail outcomes remain identical. Identical repeated executions and relocated identical applications must retain identical evidence fingerprints. Separate operational diagnostics containing host-specific details from canonical portable evidence. Preserve safe literal rendering for every untrusted field, including application/test output, observations, origin metadata and diagnostics, under the existing receipt escaping rules.

Add acceptance/regression tests for exact attribution from actual checking results, unchecked neighbors, assumptions, independent failed/passing runtime and conformance records, all proof rows unchecked, zero invented assertions, truthful missing/failed evidence, and supplied-versus-executed origin across JSON round trips and transactional replacement/clearing. Test both explicit and no-components receipt modes and legacy receipt compatibility. Test hostile text in every new rendered field. Test deterministic repeats/relocation and fingerprint sensitivity independently for source, sibling, resource, test, driver, runner/observer, model, include, requirements/resolution, bounds, sampling and observations with unchanged aggregate outcomes. Exercise actual Python/TLC-generated evidence as well as serialization/attribution unit fixtures; do not substitute invented passing records for all real execution coverage.

Update SPEC.md and README in this PR to describe the new actual-result views, provenance, origin distinction and coverage limits, retaining the public-gate limitation until integration. Foundations: D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0054, D-0158, D-0161, D-0163, D-0168, D-0169, D-0170, D-0171, D-0175, D-0177, D-0178. D-0122 requires current docs and decision citations on changed SPEC bullets. The merger records this ratified plan's execution/receipt policy using decision tooling; do not edit decisions/ or existing pins/locks. Document real-test commands; require final-head passing output before proceeding. Unavailable Docker/network checks and decision recording are Merger work, alone requiring no repair.

issues.title: Enable the sampled Python application gate and document manual adoption
issues.body:
Complete #327 after its preceding session, sampled-checking and receipt issues merge. Wire these capabilities through verify.Check, verify.Run, language routing, direct Python.Check and CLI toolchain preparation so a person can manually adopt an unchanged Python application. Finish all sampled-gate work here. Exhaustive, attempted-step and applicable larger-bound integration belongs to the separately planned issue after #327.

Replace blanket ErrComponents/ErrPythonApplication refusal for the supported capability with the shared preflight. Keep precise rejection for unsupported languages/component modes, proof selections, unsupported invocation/evidence forms and inconsistent selections. Invalid explicit configuration must never fall back to legacy execution. Reject existing-Python exhaustive and attempted-step requests explicitly before tools/installations; runtime non-sampled output cannot be accepted as sampled success. Preserve RunModel, existing ordinary and marked-file Python behavior, TypeScript and other existing paths. Update obsolete existing-Python rejection assertions in existing tests and retain rejection coverage for genuinely unsupported configurations.

Public execution must prepare one session before any code or TLC check, using staged application/driver/model/include/lock inputs for every execution, attribution and hash. Select the application's admitted dependency image once from staged application-root requirements and reuse its immutable identity/resolution evidence; never resolve again from original or verification-local paths. Route this mode to no proof tool: neither ordinary modules nor files bearing a Nagini marker reach Nagini, no proof tool is prepared by the CLI, and no annotation is required. Preserve the preceding runner's offline environment, fixed hash seed, import/startup rules, cleanup and unchanged original bytes. Direct Python.Check uses the same validated application path.

Retain all applicable design/model, statement-pin, ratification, witness, fairness, liveness and known-bug checks in the normal gate. Gate success requires those checks, successful required configured tests, complete usable execution binding and successful sampled Init/Next conformance at the ratified bounds. Missing/malformed evidence, unused/substituted targets, failed/skipped/unexecuted required tests, runtime/import errors and invalid transitions fail with check-specific diagnostics. Process exit or a plausible trace alone cannot pass. Preserve independent successful observations when another check or model obligation fails and ensure the overall verdict is false. Assemble JSON/Markdown and fingerprints through the preceding actual-result path, including the no-components path with no inferred inventory, all uncovered explicit components visible and all proof coverage unchecked. Sampled implementation evidence grants no exhaustive-state, every-step, proof or every-size claim.

Add end-to-end acceptance and real Docker integration tests that call verify.Run using actual Python and TLC on an unchanged task-lifecycle application with sibling entry code, resource reads and an installed third-party wheel through the existing dependency resolver. The valid lifecycle passes and produces accurate JSON and Markdown; a real invalid transition fails. Exercise both explicit inventory with unchecked neighboring components and omitted components. Include drivers that never call the target, only import it, or touch/call it while reporting a substitute lifecycle; runtime/import errors; failing selected tests alongside passing tests; skipped and selected-but-unexecuted tests; malformed/missing evidence; and unsupported preflight with no verification or dependency tool calls. Verify that other design/pin/ratification/witness/fairness/known-bug failures still fail the gate without erasing independent code evidence. Demonstrate no Nagini preparation/call, even with a marker, and run legacy Python, marked-file Python and TypeScript regressions.

Verify deterministic repeated runs and relocation at the full report level, sensitivity to changed source/sibling/resource/test/driver/model/include/requirements/bounds/sampling inputs and changed observations with unchanged aggregate outcomes, and byte-for-byte unchanged original sources on success, failure and cancellation. Check snapshot isolation when originals change after preparation and reuse of one image selection. Exercise the CLI verify command and its exit status/receipt outputs, and direct Python.Check routing. Orchestration doubles supplement these tests but cannot replace the real gate. Extend the real integration suite with a documented command, such as go test -tags integration ./internal/verify/ ./internal/conformance/ with an explicit application-gate test selector if needed; the requested suite must fail if prerequisites are missing rather than silently passing without Python/TLC execution. Merger work must include passing real Python/TLC/Docker output on the final PR head before the next parent issue proceeds.

Update SPEC.md and README in this PR, replacing all obsolete blanket unavailability claims for Python existing/component execution with the exact supported sampled capability and limits. Supply a usable manual adoption example with application and verification directory layout, existing and explicit component selections plus the omitted-components variant, supported unittest and driver invocations, dependency/resource files, the model and bounds, working observation/read-back driver usage, verify command, and expected passing/failing receipts. Show the real workflow for a person to ratify statements/bounds before verification; templates must not invent a ratifier, decision or pre-ratified lock. Do not fabricate ratification or edit existing pinned statements/locks. Show the no-proof behavior and that factory drafting/synthesis do not yet produce this path; exhaustive/attempt coverage remains rejected pending the next issue.

Decisions D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0047 and D-0054 ground tested existing-code conformance; D-0158, D-0168, D-0177, D-0178, D-0180 and D-0181 ground identities, invocations, staging, sessions and dependencies; D-0161, D-0163, D-0169, D-0170, D-0171 and D-0175 ground independent evidence and receipts. D-0122 requires same-change current docs and citations on changed SPEC bullets. The ratified child plan for #327 supplies the new gate execution policy until the merger records the policy and dependencies using decision tooling. Do not write decisions/ or implement proof adapters, factory drafting or synthesis. Decision recording and checks requiring unavailable Docker/network access are Merger work, alone requiring no repair; the final passing real integration output remains required before moving on.
